kind: live Qodo/GitHub proof with synthetic plan inputs

returned_findings.title: Production plan expires audit logs early
returned_findings.description: `audit_expiration_days` validates only that retention is at least one day, without applying the stated 90-day production minimum. The supplied `prod` plan therefore accepts `1` for `aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration.audit`, which would cause objects in `example-audit-prod` to expire after one day.

returned_findings.title: Retention input lacks a description
returned_findings.description: `audit_expiration_days` omits the `description` attribute required by the Terraform input-contract guidance. When automation exposes this variable, operators must infer its retention semantics and environment constraints from unrelated file comments.

returned_findings.title: Production plans allow early expiry
returned_findings.description: The `audit_expiration_days` validation accepts every positive value even though production requires at least 90 days. When CI supplies a production environment with a value from 1 through 89, the lifecycle rule passes validation and plans deletion earlier than the documented policy permits.

returned_findings.title: Production audit logs can expire early
returned_findings.description: `audit_expiration_days` validates only that retention is positive even though the configuration declares a 90-day production minimum. The supplied production plan uses 120 days, but any later `prod` value from CI between 1 and 89 passes validation and directly controls the enabled audit-bucket expiration rule.

returned_findings.title: Two inputs lack descriptions
returned_findings.description: `environment` and `audit_expiration_days` omit the descriptions required by the Terraform input-contract rule. When callers inspect or reuse this configuration, they cannot discover the expected environment naming or retention semantics from the variable interface.

returned_findings.title: Demo infrastructure can reach production
returned_findings.description: `environment` accepts any string, so the demonstration Terraform has no enforceable guard preventing a production target. When CI supplies `production` and Terraform is applied, it creates and manages a real audit bucket despite the “Never apply” comment.

returned_findings.title: Production audit logs expire early
returned_findings.description: The `audit_expiration_days` validation checks only that retention is positive, so it accepts values below the documented 90-day production minimum and passes them directly to the enabled audit-bucket lifecycle rule. With the supplied `prod` value of 7, `aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration.audit` reaches `example-audit-prod` and schedules its audit logs for deletion 83 days earlier than required.

returned_findings.title: Production audit logs can expire early
returned_findings.description: The `audit_expiration_days` validation accepts every positive value even though production retention has a 90-day minimum. When CI supplies a value below 90 for the production environment, the enabled lifecycle rule uses it to delete all matching audit objects early.

returned_findings.title: Demo infrastructure can reach production
returned_findings.description: The `environment` input accepts any string, so the demonstration configuration has no enforceable barrier against a production value. If CI supplies `production`, the demo bucket and lifecycle policy enter a production path despite the comment instructing users never to apply them.
